methods.label: Recognize consecutive numbers
methods.levelReason: Recognizing a one-unit difference between these whole numbers is appropriate for Grade 2.

candidate.annotationRationale:
The task asks for a missing part given the total 1000 and the part 999, matching cnm_p035. The retained method identifies their one-unit difference. Understanding numbers up to 10000, cnm_p053, supplies relevant background. Remove cnm_p055 and cnm_p011 because the written method performs neither decimal regrouping nor subtraction within 10. Preserve the recorded exclusion of signed-rational subtraction. This simple exercise needs no additional method or new node.

review.mathematicalCheck: Since 999 + 1 = 1000, subtracting 999 from 1000 leaves 1. The retained sentence states this decisive relationship and sufficiently explains the answer.
review.levelCheck: Recognizing consecutive whole numbers is appropriate for Grade 2. No formal algebra or regrouping procedure is needed.
review.methodDistinctness: Only one method is included, which is sufficient for this simple calculation.
